name: Asaas

webhook.algorithm: NO CRYPTOGRAPHIC SIGNATURE. Asaas sends a shared secret verbatim in the `asaas-access-token` header; you compare it to the authToken you set (or that Asaas auto-generated) on the webhook. authToken is 32–255 chars. This is bearer-token verification, NOT HMAC — generator must emit a constant-time string compare, never a digest computation. Since nothing is signed over the body, event-id dedup plus a re-fetch is mandatory.

evidence.note: Catalog import from adversarially-checked research. The scheme above is quoted from that research and has NOT been transcribed into typed fields, so PagoKit will not generate a verifier. Promoting this provider to generic or build means reading the provider docs and typing the scheme in.

credentials.note: API key sent in an `access_token` header. Sandbox and production keys are distinct. No verified prefix regex — leave null.

fees.notes: UNKNOWN for 2026. Asaas publishes per-plan pricing behind signup; no verified figure. Do not populate.

notes: The most accessible route to Pix Automático — Brazil's new recurring-payment rail — with documented webhook flows for it today. This is the provider that lets PagoKit generate a Brazilian subscription integration that does not depend on saving a card.
SDKs: No official first-party Node/Python/PHP package verified. Community wrappers exist. REST-only; generate a thin client.
Developer-experience scores are unrated placeholders (3/3); they are not used in ranking.
Overlaps: Complements pagarme rather than replacing it. Choose asaas when the use case is recurring billing on Pix Automático or boleto; choose pagarme for card installments and marketplace split.
Onboarding model was inferred during the catalog import and is not verified. Confirm it before relying on the "can this user actually get keys" filter.
